category_title: Credit recovery students with self-discipline and engagement challenges
student_description: This student struggles with self-discipline, procrastination, and social distractions, often avoiding work or missing class. They are easily overwhelmed by heavy reading and fear looking 'dumb' in front of peers. They uniquely require private one-on-one support, self-paced mastery learning with revision opportunities, and multimedia alternatives to text-heavy instruction, while strictly avoiding peer collaboration.

criteria.rationale: This student fears looking 'dumb' and will avoid asking questions if they feel exposed to peers.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly offers or utilizes a private, one-on-one communication method (e.g., direct message, email, private chat) for the student to ask questions or receive help.

criteria.rationale: The student needs second opportunities and extended deadlines to reduce stress and build competence without penalty.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly offers the opportunity to revise, retake, or review the specific assignment until the student understands the material and passes.

criteria.rationale: Peer interaction is a major distraction for this student, and collaborative assignments have proven ineffective.
criteria.check: The tutor's response strictly maintains an independent work structure and does not suggest or require peer communication, group work, or collaborative assignments.
